program: Survivor housing, trauma support and self-sufficiency
priceScope: Conditional annual whole-recipient cost divided by a limited modeled local channel; not a verified marginal gift offer or complete portfolio EV

what: Fort Bend Women’s Center supports survivors of domestic violence and sexual assault in the Houston region.
Its services combine crisis response, shelter, longer-term housing, counseling and legal advocacy.
Practical support and life-skills programs help survivors work toward safety and self-sufficiency.
strengths: Original latest returns expose inventory and event costs rather than a cheap net-expense denominator.
Dated adult housing outputs provide a narrower reference than repeated calls or shelter nights.
Housing, childcare, counseling and employment support connect clinical recovery with household resources.
reservations: Housing outputs do not establish additional safe housing, causal trauma improvement or net earnings.
Adult-household deduplication, outside grants and the Rio Bend property boundary remain uncertain.
Market-value impact ratios and monthly demand increases cannot establish marginal donor returns.

sections.what: Fort Bend Women’s Center supports survivors of domestic violence and sexual assault in the Houston region. Its services combine crisis response, shelter, longer-term housing, counseling and legal advocacy. Practical support and life-skills programs help survivors work toward safety and self-sufficiency.
sections.monitoring: Original 2025 annual report image page 4 shows 526 housing/utility-assisted individuals: 199 adults and 327 children, alongside 422 sheltered survivors, 9,763 calls and 8,111 therapy sessions. These are not disjoint or completed causal outcomes. Only the 199 adult housing/utility-assistance reference is used; nights, children, therapy sessions and hours are not added. The first 183-adult 2024 model is frozen as a diagnostic. Current monthly demand 410 versus 267 is not annual unique throughput or a doubling. Request distinct adult households, assistance persistence, actual safe housing changes, completed trauma care, incremental earnings and safety/privacy incidence.
sections.qualitative: Original latest returns expose inventory and event costs rather than a cheap net-expense denominator. Dated adult housing outputs provide a narrower reference than repeated calls or shelter nights. Housing, childcare, counseling and employment support connect clinical recovery with household resources. Housing outputs do not establish additional safe housing, causal trauma improvement or net earnings. Adult-household deduplication, outside grants and the Rio Bend property boundary remain uncertain. Market-value impact ratios and monthly demand increases cannot establish marginal donor returns. Original latest Form 990 confirms EIN 76-0032451. Rio Bend property affiliate EIN 83-1388793 is distinct and not substituted as a cheaper services denominator. Recipient-owned donor route was checked without a transaction. Capital/property cash costs and partner resources require separate marginal analysis.
sections.cost: The conditional annual partial-channel reference is $128.63 million per ten combined healthy-year welfare equivalents: 1.067133 clinical QALYs and 0.148671 signed resource equivalents. $10,000 corresponds to 0.000777 combined equivalents under proportional annual accounting, not demonstrated next-gift response. Full annual recognized recipient cost is $15,639,175. Observed 2025 199 adults receiving housing/utility assistance are a limited reference, not confirmed newly housed or completed clinical beneficiaries. Judged .9 adult-household mapping times .35 additional annual response yields 62.685 exposed households. Clinical .3 meaningful safety/trauma improvement times .06 utility for one finite year is a weak hypothesis, not validated shelter efficacy or mortality. Full one-off .0005 privacy/safety harm applies to the entire exposed union. Independent .5 resource success receives $800 net incremental usable housing/essential resources after alternative aid and benefit withdrawal plus $400 net work resources after taxes, childcare, commute and displaced earnings. Positive components separately receive overlap .5 before full $200 moving, application, attendance and foregone-pay burden: successful households net $400; others lose $200. Union 62.684999999999995 household proxies contains clinical subgroup 18.8055; no separate clinical population is added. One welfare-equivalent adult per household at $20,000 annual consumption, with components netted before one log. Positive components alone receive overlap adjustment; negative components, all unavoidable costs and union harms remain full. Clinical failure retains resource exposures and burdens. ResourceYears is fraction of one year’s gain, not repeated lifetime payments. No retail medicines, gross salaries, ordinary survivor earnings or property wealth are counted. Housing and donated goods are not automatically new net social resources. Matched payer/displaced-beneficiary stress applies only to truly additional budget or displacement, not identical recipient grants charged twice. Provider burden is independently stressed. Property-affiliate and volunteer opportunity resources are unknown centrally, and central payer/provider zero is not observed zero or complete world benefit. Central partner/payer zero is unknown-neutral, not observed zero or complete world net benefit. Other programs and external opportunity costs remain unknown; whole recipient cost versus this narrow channel is not complete portfolio EV or a marginal gift offer.
sections.funding: FY2025 original tax expense $12,537,293 plus $83,678 direct event cost and $3,018,204 netted inventory cost gives $15,639,175. FY2024 $11,224,046 plus $32,828 and $2,694,431 gives $13,951,305. FY2023 $10,895,549 plus $100,102 and $2,746,340 gives $13,741,991. The inventory resource cost is included once, not also credited at retail value to households. No populated expense-side donated addback recovered; this is not proof of zero outside resources. Full recognized annual services recipient versus current narrow adult housing/utility-assistance numerator has an explicit whole-recipient/partial-channel scope mismatch. The public $8–$10 community benefit ratio, retail counseling value and avoided rental subsidy valuation are not used as clinical or household consumption estimates.

sources.title: Current survivor shelter and practical support mechanisms

model.costScope: Whole recognized annual services recipient resources versus narrow current adult housing/utility-assistance recovery channel; other portfolio and marginal gift unknown
model.geographicAttribution: Fort Bend County and Houston MSA support; .98 local share judged, not measured household residence
model.formula: Union=N*unique*b; clinical=union*completion*q*discounted finite years minus full union harms. Financial=.5*people*discounted one-year log(1+joint net gain/baseline), local share once. Headline=10*C/(clinical+financial).
model.counterfactual: Existing public grants, victim compensation, other shelter/housing/counseling providers, employment programs and family support retained
model.attribution: Annual incremental recipient response is distinct from cohort deduplication and geographic share; no claim of whole annual portfolio or marginal donation causal effect.
model.uncertainty: Source-grounded original cost/services; all causal mapping, utility and net resource priors unsupported. Complete portfolio and marginal donor EV unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: Additional housing/utility security and trauma recovery plus usable net household resources; not shelter nights, market therapy value or gross wages
